name: codex-orchestration
description: Fast Terra-first numeric routing across seven model lanes.

interface.shortDescription: Fast credit routing with one numeric score
interface.longDescription: Activate Codex Orchestration for the current chat with Turn Orchestration on, Use Orchestration, or Use Orchestration for this chat. Its stable user-level runtime hook runs once per prompt and sends up to 64 recent turns from that chat only to GPT-5.6 Terra / High without loading a routing skill or generating a receipt. It uses a deliberately partial context fork so pinned roles also work in a brand-new task; on short tasks, the one omitted oldest task turn is copied verbatim. Terra returns one immutable complexity score from 1.0 to 10.0 plus one concise visible checkpoint. Below 5.0, root delegates directly from that score. From 5.0 through 7.9, Sol / High may add only a NONE or 60-word decision directive; at 8.0 or above, that executive is Sol / Extra High. The original task context goes directly to the implementer, so executives never spend output tokens rewriting the request, deployment workflow, or acceptance criteria. The user-selected root is a zero-judgment relay and alone performs agent handoffs. The one selected implementation role must perform the work itself and cannot create Recon, reviewer, helper, replacement, or other nested subagents. Seven implementation lanes are used: Luna / Max at 1.0–2.9, Terra / Medium at 3.0–5.0, Terra / High at 5.1–6.5, Sol / Low at 6.6–7.2, Sol / Medium at 7.3–7.9, Sol / High at 8.0–8.9, and Sol / Extra High at 9.0–10.0. Terra owns acceptance below 5.0; Sol / High owns it from 5.0 through 7.9 and Sol / Extra High owns it at 8.0 and above, so any user-selected starting model is safe. Producer claims are untrusted: the executive independently probes code and deployed state. Routine frontend acceptance relies on code, tests, and the deployed revision; visual tools are used only when the user explicitly requests visual inspection, reports a rendered mismatch, or visual input is indispensable to perform the work. An access-path or pre-execution command-construction failure is not an outcome failure: acceptance uses its one fallback call through a corrected or authoritative read-only runtime path and never performs user-reserved mutations. Root always appends the executive route, implementation route, and immutable complexity lines to the final response; on takeover it reads the active task context and reports the exact root model and effort instead of a generic default. Executive and implementation task names are distinct. Routine Git and SSH deployment does not itself force escalation. Steering drains only the active Orchestration branch before rescoring, and completed side effects are reconciled rather than assumed rolled back. Any failed or incomplete implementation or acceptance ends routing immediately; the user-selected root model reconciles actual state and finishes the entire request directly with no more handoffs.
defaultPrompt: Tell me “Turn Orchestration on” for same-chat, score-based routing across seven model lanes.
